subject: CareBridge — dedicated capacity alignment and next steps
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@carebridge.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@carebridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: CareBridge — dedicated capacity alignment and next steps

Alex — thanks again for a productive conversation earlier. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum. I tried to capture pain, goals, and an initial configuration that fits what you described. Please flag anything I got wrong.

1) What you told us (pain & impact)
- Bursty peaks from inference jobs (image-heavy clinical triage) cause 300–500ms latency spikes and missed SLAs during morning batch windows.
- Mixed-sensitivity data: PHI in inference payloads, requirement to limit cross-tenant surface area.
- Current ops overhead: engineers maintain spot instances and custom autoscaling; want predictability and a single SLA-backed endpoint for product teams.

2) Your goals
- Predictable latency under 150ms p50 for interactive model paths, 99.9% availability for inference endpoints, and predictable monthly spend for product forecasting.
- Strong tenant isolation (dedicated pool or single-tenant option) for a subset of internal workflows that process PHI.
- Easy integration with existing KMS and VPC peering for audit/compliance.

3) Proposed Redwood dedicated configuration (initial)
- Reserved pool: 8x A100 40GB (or equivalent A800 if preferred) dedicated to CareBridge — supports concurrent interactive throughput ~120 reqs/s with automatic KV cache and batching.
- Isolation: dedicated pool with single-tenant assignment for PHI workloads + policy-based routing for non-PHI to a shared pool.
- Burst policy: 30% burst capacity (soft) for scheduled morning pipelines; automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant if capacity constrained.
- SLA targets: 99.9% availability SLA for reserved pool; 150ms p50 latency target for interactive requests at expected QPS.
- Observability: per-route token-level breakdown, trace IDs for request reconstruction, and audit logs retained per your retention policy.

4) Commercial and procurement notes (ballpark)
- Estimated monthly commit for the above config: $XXk–$YYk/mo depending on term (12 vs 36 months) and HW selection. I will route a formal commercial once we lock sizing.

5) Next steps / asks
- You: confirm that PHI + non-PHI separation approach looks viable and share procurement contact (you already copied Jordan — thanks).
- Us: we’ll produce a one-page isolation diagram, a detailed capacity worksheet (attached), and example SLA language.
- Schedule: if this matches, recommend a technical deep-dive with our solutions engineer (30–45m) to validate throughput numbers and failure/fallback behavior.

Attachments: CareBridge_RI_dedicated_plan_v1.pdf (overview) and capacity_config.xlsx (workload inputs).

If agreeable, I’ll also attach SOC2 evidence and our standard security questionnaire in the next email for Jordan/procurement.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

Thanks Mateo — helpful summary. A few quick confirmations and asks from our side: 

- The pain and goals summary is correct. Main priority is isolation for PHI workflows and predictable cost.
- For compliance: we will need SOC 2 Type II docs, an explicit KMS/HSM integration path, and confirmation that audit logs include per-request metadata for at least 12 months.
- Procurement: Jordan Lee (cc) will be the primary PO contact; procurement@carebridge.ai is our shared inbox for redlines and third-party vendor forms.

Jordan — can you confirm the vendor onboarding timeline and whether you need an initial quote or an NDA before we share compliance docs?

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the plan. Happy to set the technical deep-dive for Thursday if Mateo/your team is available.

—Alex
VP Product | CareBridge AI
alex.johnson@carebridge.ai

Thanks — Mateo
